title: Siena no. 11: Donato Acciaiuoli to Lorenzo de' Medici, Rome, 13 June 1478 (ASSi Concistoro 2308 fasc. 2 no. 11, DECODE R4800)

steps.what: Project survey (siena1421): no. 11 transcribed from the DECODE photographs by agent B (409 tokens, 44 sign names).
Project survey: homophonic annealing on the 409 tokens; no convergence.
Project survey: Sienese key R4752 ('Cifra de m. Antonio Bichi 1478 Rom.') compared; does not fit. Gabbrielli's Florentine key index (Ilardi reel 58) has no key for Donato Acciaiuoli in 1478.
George Lasry's session: 393 cipher symbols transcribed by Claude in CTTS.
George Lasry with CTTS and Claude: key recovered by Claude by crib analysis from the ciphertext; 57 signs, homophonic; both blocks read, about 90% certain; two encipherer's slips marked.
This project counted George Lasry's reading: 357 of 381 plaintext letters (93.7%) in words without a query mark; one sign lost in a hole.

No. 11: his key on the project's own 24 Sept transcription (transcripts/no11.txt, agent B): 66.7% with 8 signs unidentified, 94.4% (357/378 sign units) once his two-stroke signs '+o' = e and 'o+' = d are read as our token pairs PLUS O / O PLUS and ODAG = h, D = a, RHO = o; his nulls 'g#', '31', '87', m^n, /// are our G HASH, 3 1, 8^dot 7, M^n, SL3. Our two cipher blocks are his two runs line for line. research/siena2308/verify_lasry.py no11.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): George Lasry's decryption and translation in lasry_report.md, the project's own 24 Sept transcription transcripts/no11.txt (his CTTS transcription is not in the repository), his key as counts in key.md.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): lasry_report.md read: both cipher blocks build sentences and translate; the doubts are one holed sign and five words, with outside blockers. Per-document C overturned to B. Claim unchanged.

texts.label: No. 11 (R4800), Donato Acciaiuoli to Lorenzo de' Medici, Rome, 13 June 1478 (George Lasry)
texts.summary: Donato Acciaiuoli, Florentine orator in Rome, to Lorenzo de' Medici, seven weeks after the Pazzi conspiracy: the lord of Faenza, like the lord of Forlì, is to stay in his lands and send two squadrons of men-at-arms into the field, and Giovan Francesco Gonzaga will gladly enter Lorenzo's service with at least 80 men-at-arms, asking 7,000 ducats for the troops and 1,000 for himself. Decryption and translation are George Lasry's (report of 17 Oct 2026, quoted whole); the transcription linked is this project's independent one of 24 Sept 2026, on which his key was checked (94.4% agreement), since his own sign-level CTTS transcription is not in the repository.

reading_review.note: Overturns the per-document C. Both blocks of Lasry's decryption build Italian sentences with an English translation; the "?" fall in one sentence of block A, around one sign lost in a hole in the paper (illegible), and in five single words of a 393-sign text (too short to settle), both outside blockers.

prior.where: No decipherment on DECODE or in print known; the project's 24 Sept survey left it unread.

human: George Lasry ran the solution in CTTS with Claude (transcription by Claude, key recovered by Claude by crib analysis); this project filed his report and counted his reading.
